name: okliterun
description: A lightweight one-click code runner for VS Code (preview). Inspired by Code Runner.

virtualWorkspaces.description: OkLiteRun executes files on a local or remote machine.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: OkLiteRun runs workspace code and stays disabled until the workspace is trusted.

okliterun.runInTerminal.markdownDescription: Run in the integrated terminal so programs can read stdin (`input()`, `scanf`, and similar). When this is off, OkLiteRun captures stdout and stderr in an output channel and does not provide stdin.

enumDescriptions: Use the directory of the file being run.
Use the workspace folder that contains the file.

okliterun.saveBeforeRun.description: Save the active file before running it. Untitled files still run from a temporary copy if you cancel the save dialog, only when this is off.

okliterun.clearPreviousOutput.description: Clear the terminal (or the output channel) before each run.

okliterun.preserveFocus.description: Keep focus in the editor after starting a run. Leave this off when the program reads stdin.

okliterun.pythonPath.markdownDescription: Python executable. When empty, OkLiteRun uses the Python extension's selected interpreter, then `python3`, then `python` (and `py` on Windows).

okliterun.executorMap.markdownDescription: Per-language command overrides, keyed by VS Code language id (`python`, `javascript`, `typescript`, `c`, `cpp`, `java`, `go`, `php`, `shellscript`, `powershell`, …). Placeholders are quoted for the active terminal shell: `$file`, `$fileNoExt`, `$dir`, `$fileName`, `$fileNameNoExt`, `$workspaceRoot`, `$exe`, `$python`. Do not add your own quotes around placeholders. Separate compile-and-run steps with ` && ` (spaces around `&&`). Example: `{ "python": "$python -u $file" }`.
